status: THE STORED RATE LIBRARY IS WITHDRAWN. This file carries no prices and never will. It carries the item taxonomy a market search needs, and the three market-independent guards that replace the withdrawn library's min/max envelope.

provenance.taxonomy: the item classes of reference/rate-library.md, prices stripped. The taxonomy is a classification of work; the prices were a 2026 snapshot and are withdrawn.
provenance.guard_replaced: reference/quantity-reconciliation-gates.md G+.32, whose envelope was drawn from the library
provenance.why: the library's failure mode was silent: bulk excavation priced at the raft concrete rate, a 5.0M overstatement, because a keyword matched. Withdrawing the library removes the envelope that caught it, so the envelope is replaced rather than dropped.

currency.foreign_source: a source quoting another currency records the FX pair, the rate used and the date of that rate. An unconverted foreign figure never reaches a bill row.

assignment.rule: a rate class is assigned from the POMI clause being billed plus the element's stated attributes. NEVER from keyword or regex matching on the description text.
forbidden: matching a description string to a class name
a rate with no source URL
a rate with no retrieval date
a rate whose quoted unit differs from the row's unit
averaging observations drawn from different classes
carrying a rate across projects without re-searching
assignment.unlisted_class: a class absent from this table is created at run time from the clause and the element attributes, searched on its own terms, and flagged UNLISTED_CLASS for the reviewer.

search.budget: one search per distinct rate class per run, cached. Never per bill line.

corroboration.independence: distinct registrable domains. Two pages of one publisher are one source.
corroboration.published_value: the median of the corroborating observations
corroboration.on_single_source: flag SINGLE_SOURCE. The row is priced but cannot be issued until a reviewer clears it.
corroboration.on_no_source: the row is a gap, not a number. Invariant: gaps are never assumptions.

spread.on_breach: flag CLASS_SPREAD. A spread this wide usually means the search pulled two different items into one class - split the class and search again rather than taking the median.
spread.note: the ratio is deliberately generous. It is a class-coherence test, not a price-accuracy test.

bands.action: accept, escalate by the stated rule, flag ESCALATED
reject the source - it cannot bound a current rate

staleness.escalation_rule: 3 to 5 per cent per year, straight-line, applied by stated rule and never by judgement. The run states which figure it used and why, per class.
staleness.no_price_date: a source that does not state when its price was current is rejected. A rate with no date cannot be escalated.

ordinal_invariants.why: these orderings follow from what the work is, not from what it costs, so they hold in every market at every date. They are what survives the library's withdrawal, and they catch the exact failure G+.32 was built for: excavation priced at a concrete rate breaks invariant 2.
ordinal_invariants.on_breach: FAIL. Both classes are re-searched. If the breach survives the re-search it is a manual rate assignment with a written note - never a silent acceptance.

share_guard.rule: no single priced row may exceed 35 per cent of its section total without a written note in AN.RECONCILIATION
share_guard.why: the library failure was detected as a 5.0M overstatement in one row. A share test catches that symptom even when every other gate passes.

regional_adjustment.apply: only where the corroborating sources state a region other than the project's, and then disclosed per row
regional_adjustment.never: applied on top of a rate already sourced in the project's own emirate
regional_adjustment.note: carried from reference/rate-library.md's adjustment table. These are market-structure statements, not prices, so they survive the library's withdrawal. A range is applied at its midpoint and the midpoint is disclosed.
